title: Free AI meeting notes: a recording transcribed on your device · {name}
description: Drop a meeting recording in a browser tab: its words are written on your device, then AI makes the minutes, decisions and actions. Free, nothing to install.
h1: Turn a recording into meeting notes, heard on your own device.
acts: Turn a recording into meeting notes,
lede: Drop a recording of a meeting, an interview or a voice memo in {name}. What is said in it is written down in this tab, a line each half minute with its time. Then ask for the minutes: what was decided, who does what by when, what is still open. The sound is never sent to an AI.
cta.note: There is no sample recording: bring one of yours, a voice memo of a minute to start with, and drop it in the box. The first time, {name} asks before it downloads what writes speech down.
pane.title: A recording’s minutes, written in {name}
demo.answer:
Here are the minutes, from what was said in the recording. Each point gives its time.

## Decided

- The shop opens on Sunday mornings from 1 June, on trial until the end of August ({t1}).
- The spring catalogue goes to print: 500 copies for €480 ({t2}).

## Who does what

| Who | What | By when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inès | Write the Sunday rota | 15 May |
| Marc | Send the catalogue’s files to the printer | Friday |
| Sofia | Ask the town hall about the terrace | 12 May |

## Still open

- Hiring for the summer: no decision, back on the agenda on 12 May ({t4}).

The next meeting is on 12 May, at the same time ({t5}). A recording doesn’t say who is speaking: I took the names from what people said, so check them.
heard.lines: OK, it’s the 5th of May and everyone is here. Three things today: opening on Sundays, the spring catalogue, and staff for the summer.
So we agree, we open on Sunday mornings from the 1st of June, on trial until the end of August. Inès, can you write the rota by the 15th? Yes, I’ll do it.
The printer’s quote is 480 euros for 500 copies. That’s fine, let’s go. Marc, you send him the files by Friday.
For the terrace we need the town hall’s answer first. Sofia, will you ask them before the next meeting? I’ll call them this week.
On hiring for the summer, I don’t think we can decide today. Let’s put it back on the agenda for the 12th.
Next meeting on the 12th of May, same time. Thanks, everyone.

exact.title: Written down here, not in the cloud.
exact.why: Most tools send your recording to a server to be transcribed. {name} writes it down in this tab, then hands the AI words alone.
exact.cards: What writes speech down runs on your own computer or phone. It is downloaded once, with your agreement: 18 MB in English, German, French, Spanish, Italian and Dutch, about 80 MB in other languages.
Each line starts with its time in the recording, so the notes can say when a thing was said, and you can go and hear it.
The AI you chose reads the words, as it would read a document. It doesn’t need to hear, and the sound is not sent to it.
where.title: Where your recording goes.
where.why: It stays with you. Only its words go to the AI that answers, and you choose it.
where.cards: The recording and its words stay in your browser, encrypted. Nothing we can read reaches us.
Only words, to the AI you chose
Your request and what was said go to the AI you picked, and nowhere else. Under every answer, {name} says where it was done.
With the AI on this computer, the words don’t leave it either: the one for a board meeting or a job interview. It needs 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. Without a sign-up, only the AI on this computer answers.
It doesn’t tell speakers apart: the words come as one text. Names in the notes come from what people say, so check who took what.
It doesn’t join a call or record one: record with your phone or your call software, then bring the file.
Words can be misheard, names and figures first, and {name} can be wrong. Check the notes against the recording.
It writes in the language {name} is set to: a meeting held in two languages comes out poorly.
It runs on your own device, so a long meeting takes a while, longer on an old laptop. A file holds 100 MB at most.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for, or the AI on this computer, with no account at all.
No. It is written down in this tab, and stays on your devices. Only its words go to the AI you chose; with the AI on this computer, nothing leaves it.
Sound as MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, Opus, FLAC, AAC or WebM, and films as MP4 or MOV, up to 100 MB each.
Does it say who is speaking?
No. What is said comes as one text, with times. Where people name each other, the notes can say who took a task.
The one {name} is set to. English, German, French, Spanish, Italian and Dutch use a small download, 18 MB; other languages a larger one, about 80 MB.
Can it record the meeting for me?
No. Record it with your phone, a recorder or your call software, then drop the file in the box.
